response_text:
The main alternatives to **DonorBox** fall into three groups: full fundraising suites (e.g., RallyUp, Givebutter, Bloomerang), lightweight/low-fee platforms (e.g., Zeffy, Fundly, Donately), and WordPress donation plugins (e.g., GiveWP, Paymattic). The best choice depends on whether you prioritize fees, events, CRM, or WordPress integration.

Below is a concise comparison of leading options so you can quickly narrow down a shortlist.

---

### 1. All‑in‑one fundraising platforms (similar use cases to DonorBox)

These are best if you want campaigns, events, some automation, and possibly CRM in one place.

| Platform | Why choose it instead of DonorBox? | Fees / Pricing (platform only) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **RallyUp** | **Most comprehensive DonorBox replacement** with campaigns, P2P, raffles, auctions, galas, and text‑to‑give in one tool.[3] | Free plan (funded by donor tips), or 2.9–6.9% “Flex” fees depending on activity.[3] |
| **Givebutter** | All‑in‑one fundraising (campaigns, events, ticketing, auctions, livestreaming) plus simple CRM; very transparent pricing.[3][6] | 0% platform fee with tips on; ~3% when tips off; paid “Plus” from $29/mo.[3] |
| **Zeffy** | **Only truly 0% platform + 0% processing fee option** for nonprofits; supports events, raffles, auctions, forms; funded entirely by optional donor tips.[3][2] | Always 0% to you; donors are *asked* (but not forced) to tip Zeffy.[3][2] |
| **Bloomerang Giving Platform** | Combines fundraising tools with a more robust **donor CRM and volunteer management**, aimed at growing relationships, not just transactions.[1][3] | Forms at $0; P2P/auctions from $259/mo; text fundraising add‑on; ~3.95% processing.[3] |
| **OneCause** | Strong for **auctions, galas, and in‑person events** plus text‑to‑give; good for orgs that are very event‑driven.[3] | PAYG ~5% + upfront fee for small orgs, or annual contracts from ~$2,995.[3] |
| **GoFundMe Pro (formerly Classy)** | Good if you want GoFundMe’s brand reach plus advanced nonprofit tools and peer‑to‑peer.[3][6] | Contracted pricing; processing usually ~2.4–2.9%.[3] |
| **Fundraise Up** | Optimized donation forms with **AI‑driven conversion tools and A/B testing**, best for larger orgs focused on maximizing online revenue.[3][9] | Custom; often ~4.9% platform + processing.[3] |

If you liked DonorBox’s *versatility* but want more event tools or better pricing, start comparisons with **RallyUp**, **Givebutter**, and **Zeffy**.[3][2]

---

### 2. Lower‑cost / simpler donation platforms

These are focused on online forms and campaigns, without heavy event or CRM features.

| Platform | Highlights vs DonorBox | Pricing snapshot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Donately** | Designed specifically as a **DonorBox alternative for small nonprofits**, emphasizing customizable forms and simpler setup.[10][3] | 4% on standard plan; 2% on $99/mo plan; 0% if you prepay for a $5k processing pool, plus 2.2–2.9% processing.[3] |
| **Fundly** | Easy online crowdfunding and peer‑to‑peer, good social sharing; lighter‑weight than full suites.[3][2] | 0% platform fee (funded via donor tips) + 2.9% + $0.30 processing.[3][2] |
| **ActBlue** (for US progressive causes) | Purpose‑built for political and progressive causes; simple forms with massive donor network.[3] | 3.95% processing + $0.30 per donation, no monthly fees.[3] |
| **Flipcause** | Integrated events plus volunteer management; better for orgs that need volunteer tools alongside donations.[3] | ~$125–$200/mo with processing 6.9% + $0.30 but capped at 1.5% effective rate.[3] |

If you mainly want **clean forms and recurring giving** with simpler pricing than DonorBox, **Donately** and **Fundly** are the closest replacements.[3][10]

---

### 3. WordPress‑based alternatives (if you collect donations on your own WP site)

If your site runs on WordPress and you liked embedding DonorBox forms, these plugins keep everything native.

| Plugin | Why use it | Notable details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **GiveWP** | One of the most widely used and well‑reviewed WordPress donation plugins; deep form customization and reporting.[4][9] | 100k+ active installs; flat‑rate add‑on pricing; good for orgs that want control over design and data.[4] |
| **Paymattic** | Markets itself as a **best DonorBox alternative for non‑profits using WordPress**, with easy donation forms and broad payment gateway support.[4] | Supports 135+ currencies and 11 gateways; all donations are processed directly on your site.[4] |
| **Charitable** | Lower‑cost plugin focused on giving powerful donation tools “without a high price tag.”[4] | Premium starts around $119 per site; good for small orgs that want one‑time + recurring giving.[4] |
| **WP Crowdfunding** | Ideal if you want **crowdfunding style** campaigns (multiple projects, backer pages) in WordPress.[4] | Built on WooCommerce; more of a Kickstarter‑style model than simple donations.[4] |

Pick this route if your priorities are **owning your data, tight design control, and avoiding a hosted platform**.

---

### 4. CRM‑first systems that include donation tools

If you are outgrowing DonorBox and need more advanced donor management, these are worth considering.

| Platform | Positioning | When it makes sense |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bloomerang CRM** | Donor management + fundraising pages, email, events, and volunteer tools in one.[1][6] | For organizations ready to unify email, events, and giving in a central donor database. |
| **Bonterra Network for Good, DonorPerfect, Neon CRM** | Full donor CRMs with integrated online giving and events.[6] | When you need robust reporting, segmentation, and long‑term donor stewardship on top of donation forms. |
| **Raiser’s Edge NXT** | Enterprise‑grade fundraising CRM.[6] | Large nonprofits with complex development operations and multiple revenue streams. |

These are best if your pain point with DonorBox is **data fragmentation or limited donor analytics**, not just fees.

---

### 5. How to choose an alternative (quick decision guide)

Ask yourself:

1. **Do you mainly care about lower fees?**  
   - Nonprofits: look first at **Zeffy** (true 0%)[3][2] and **Givebutter** (0% with tips).[3]  
   - Individuals or informal campaigns: **Fundly**, **Spotfund**, **Bonfire** if you want merch.[2][3]

2. **Are events, auctions, or galas central to your fundraising?**  
   - Strong event tools: **RallyUp**, **OneCause**, **GiveSmart**, **Bloomerang Fundraising**.[3]  
   - Auctions‑heavy: **Auctria**, **RallyUp**, **Givebutter**.[3]

3. **Do you want a full donor CRM built in?**  
   - Consider **Bloomerang CRM**, **Network for Good**, **Neon CRM**, **DonorPerfect**, or **Raiser’s Edge NXT** depending on your size and budget.[1][6]

4. **Is your website WordPress and you want to stay on‑site?**  
   - Choose **GiveWP**, **Paymattic**, **Charitable**, or **WP Crowdfunding**.[4]

5. **Are you a very small or new nonprofit needing simplicity?**  
   - Start with **Zeffy**, **Givebutter**, or **Donately**; they are easy to set up and well‑documented.[3][10]

---

If you share your org size, whether you use WordPress, and roughly how much you process per year, I can recommend 2–3 specific DonorBox alternatives that are likely the best fit and outline a migration approach.
